title: Normalize control-plane ownership: create tenant_ownership table and perform online migration
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Summary:
We have multiple caller-facing tables (tenants, projects, allocations, audit_logs) that encode ownership information in polymorphic columns (owner_type, owner_id) or duplicated tenant_fk columns spread across shards. These patterns complicate joins, prevent stable foreign key constraints, and drive a class of slow ad-hoc JOIN queries observed in control-plane dashboards. The goal of this ticket is to introduce a normalized tenant_ownership table, migrate reads and writes to reference it, add appropriate indexes and constraints, and perform the change online with zero downtime and a clear rollback path.

Motivation and impact:
- Removes polymorphic lookup patterns that force repeated index scans.
- Enables declarative FK constraints to improve data integrity and simplify future refactors.
- Reduces cardinality surprises in planner leading to 10-40% faster multi-join control-plane queries in internal dashboards and route builders.
- Low-to-medium customer impact if done carefully; migration will be staged and monitored.

Scope & goals (MVP):
1) Add tenant_ownership table: columns (id UUID, tenant_id UUID, owner_type TEXT, owner_id UUID, created_at TIMESTAMP, source TEXT) with unique constraint on (owner_type, owner_id) and index on tenant_id.
2) Backfill ownership rows for existing polymorphic refs and duplicated tenant_fks.
3) Convert critical query paths (allocation listing, audit log author lookups, rollout resolution) to join tenant_ownership instead of polymorphic joins.
4) Add FK constraints where safe and create a phased column deprecation plan to remove legacy owner_type/owner_id fields.
5) Instrument dashboards and runbook for migration and performance regressions.

Design considerations and trade-offs:
- We intentionally do not collapse ownership into a single denormalized column to avoid wide row bloat and to preserve provenance (source column).
- We will keep polymorphic columns readable for one cycle after backfill and make writes dual-write for a transitional period to allow rollback. Dual-write increases transient write latency risk; we will gate dual-write behind feature flag and limit to control-plane services during the migration window.
- Adding FK constraints may require index builds on very large tables; use CONCURRENTLY where supported and schedule low-traffic windows for heavy DDL.

Migration plan (phased):
Phase 0: Audit (2 days)
- Run analytics queries to enumerate owner_type/owner_id value distributions and identify top 95% of join paths.
- Baseline dashboard latencies and explain plans for target queries.
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwoodai.com/display/CPDB/tenant-ownership-design (draft).

Phase 1: Schema and backfill (3-5 days)
- Create tenant_ownership table in a migration (non-blocking pattern).
- Backfill via idempotent job (k8s job + batching), write progress to a migration_progress table.
- Validate row counts and run checksum queries.
- Links: GH - https://github.com/redwood-inference/control-plane/pull/3421 (backfill job), dashboard - https://grafana.redwoodai.com/d/gbn7/control-plane-joins

Phase 2: Read migration and canary (2 days)
- Deploy service changes that switch specific read paths to join tenant_ownership; start with internal admin routes and then small customer-facing routes.
- Monitor latency, error rates, and DB cpu.

Phase 3: Dual-write & constraint enforcement (3 days)
- Enable dual-write: all writes populate tenant_ownership and keep legacy columns for 1 business cycle.
- After stable window, add FK constraints CONCURRENTLY and drop legacy write paths behind feature flag.

Phase 4: Cleanup (1-2 days)
- Remove polymorphic columns and associated partial indexes.
- Update docs and run final data consistency checks.

Operational runbook and monitoring:
- Migration will be guarded by a dedicated runbook (runbook doc link: https://docs.redwoodai.com/runbooks/tenant-ownership-migration).
- Create Grafana panels: backfill progress, join latency P50/P95, DB CPU, lock wait events, deadlocks.
- Set Prometheus alerts for >15% latency regression on target endpoints, deadlocks, or >10% unexpected error rate.

Rollbacks and safety nets:
- During read canary, we will revert reads to legacy behavior via simple feature flag.
- Dual-write allows full rollback by switching reads back while leaving tenant_ownership rows intact (idempotent).
- Backfill job tracks checkpoints per table so re-run is safe.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for migration SQL and ORM layer.
- Integration test in staging with a realistic snapshot (5% production size) and the migration enabled.
- Load test in performance cluster to ensure no regression under typical query mix.

Open questions & next steps:
- Confirm maximum safe window for concurrent index builds with infra (ask infra team for preferred windows).
- Decide TTL for source column and retention policy for retired columns.
- Verify cross-region replication implications for FK constraints.

Deliverables & acceptance criteria:
- tenant_ownership table exists and backfill completes for >99% of rows referenced by top-95% queries.
- No user-visible errors during canary; P95 latency for target endpoints within 10% of baseline or improved.
- FK constraints added and legacy polymorphic columns dropped after verification.
- PRs merged and migration recorded in release controlplane-2025.03.
